findings.summary: docs/system-facts.md is not among the reading's deliverables
findings.evidence: A change outside the listed deliverables widens the scope.

findings.summary: The pinned critic phrase "raise a major finding" is already in today's critic.md, so it does not tie the major severity to the new item.
findings.evidence: critic.md line 14 already reads "In round one, raise a major finding when a step calls an external service...", and the existing test at lib.rs:476 pins it. A critic bullet that dropped the major severity but kept "commit-shape table" would still pass the new test. Fix: Pin a phrase that joins the severity to the new rule, for example "raise a major finding when a landing, history or attribution plan lacks", instead of the bare "raise a major finding".
findings.location: Steps 1 and 4 (critic pinned phrases); Demonstration for criterion 3

findings.summary: The new 900-token bound leaves the planner frame only about 30 tokens (about 90 bytes) of room, so a slightly longer bullet fails the test.
findings.evidence: The plan estimates the planner frame at about 640 tokens and the bullet at about 230 (700 bytes), which ends near 870, against a limit of 900. The "keep it near 700 bytes" in step 2 is a soft target. Fix: Have the producer measure the frame after editing (cargo test -p athena-context prints the failure) and choose the bound from the measured size plus a stated margin. Or set a hard cap on the bullet's size in step 2.

findings.summary: The list of five shapes is worded differently in Files and in Step 1, which is the exact pinned phrase.
findings.evidence: Files says "job commits, records-only, owner-path, intervention, retry-after-block landing". Step 1 pins "job commits, records-only, owner-path, intervention and retry-after-block landing". Fix: Use Step 1's wording everywhere so the producer copies the version the test pins.

summary: The plan fixes the cause where it starts. It puts a commit-shape table rule and a realistic-fixture rule in planner.md and a matching major-finding item in critic.md, then pins both with a new test next to the existing pattern in crates/athena-context/src/lib.rs (external_service_calls_need_a_named_state_and_a_wait, lines 462-486). I read the snapshot to check what it names. PLANNER_FRAME and CRITIC_FRAME are include_str! consts at lib.rs:56-65. The 700-token bound is at lib.rs:404. In crates/athena-cli/tests/budgets.rs, system_facts_budgets_match_computed (line 125) prints the computed value on failure, as step 5 expects. Grepping for PLANNER_FRAME, CRITIC_FRAME, planner.md and critic.md found the readers the plan lists: planning.rs:136/289, the run/mod.rs import, the briefs.rs pins at 2643-2675, headroom_rows (lib.rs:284-293, covered by the headroom test), and refusal_corpus.rs:167. Every reader of docs/system-facts.md I found (status.rs BUILD_PATHS, xtask BUILD_INPUT_GLOBS, SYSTEM_FACTS) uses it as a path or embeds it whole, so changing two numbers breaks none of them. The scope change to system-facts.md is forced by the budgets test and the plan explains why; Athena already flagged it as minor. The approach is sound: the five-shape list is extended from HISTORY.txt rather than fixed, and the plan openly marks the guard as prose pinned by a test. I found two minor weaknesses in the test: one pinned critic phrase is already in critic.md, and the raised frame bound leaves the planner little room. Neither leaves a criterion unshown.
